Organization scoping
Every user belongs to a Keycloak Organization. NCP offerings carry
provider_organization_id , so NCP users only see their own organization’s inventory and
requests.
Platform Admins see across all NCPs.
Only account-manager roles may be in multiple organizations (enforced by the multi-org-
policy  Keycloak extension).
One organization exists per Salesforce partner account; NCP organization names come from
the Salesforce account name.
Customer conﬁdentiality
NCPs may see a customer’s organization name blurred and labelled Conﬁdential until
engagement. Contracted prices are only visible to NCPs, platform account managers and admins.
Account status gates
After login, the backend middleware and frontend middleware check, in order:
1. Access denied — identity veriﬁed but not authorized (for example personal email domain,
missing role). User is pinned to /access-denied .
2. Access pending — the user’s email domain belongs to an NVIDIA partner but the NCP has
not been onboarded yet. An access request is created and the user waits on /access-pending
until a Platform Admin approves.
3. User status PENDING — account awaiting activation; user sees /user-status-pending
(“Thanks for Signing up”).
4. Proﬁle incomplete — user must ﬁll Complete Your Proﬁle (ﬁrst name, last name,
organization name, phone).
5. Terms not accepted — a blocking modal requires scrolling the Terms and Conditions, ticking
“I have read and agree to the Terms and Conditions” and clicking Accept & Continue.
User account statuses are ACTIVE  and PENDING .
Why is a menu item missing?
Menu items appear only when you hold the matching scope. For example, Upload Capacities
needs manage_inventory ; Global Capacity Explorer needs global_capacity_view . If something is
missing, ask your Platform Admin to grant the role. NCP basic users ( provider_basic_user ) are read-
only by design and are sent to the table view instead of the split Manage reservation view.
